statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail). The length of r is exactly len(puzzles): len(r) = len(puzzles). For every i with 0 <= i < len(puzzles), r[i] equals the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(words) such that the word words[j] is valid for the puzzle puzzles[i], where a word w is valid for a puzzle p if and only if (1) w contains p[0] (there exists k with 0 <= k < len(w) and w[k] = p[0]) and (2) every byte of w occurs in p (for every k with 0 <= k < len(w), there exists l with 0 <= l < len(p) and w[k] = p[l]).
preconditions: words and puzzles are slices of byte vectors. 0 <= len(words) <= 10^5 and 0 <= len(puzzles) <= 10^4. Every byte occurring in any word or puzzle is a lowercase ASCII letter ('a' through 'z'). Every puzzle is non-empty: for every i with 0 <= i < len(puzzles), len(puzzles[i]) >= 1.
